Compared with other nonlipid nanocarriers, including polymeric nanoparticles and inorganic systems that often face challenges related to biodegradability, toxicity, or large-scale manufacturing, NanoVac combines scalable production with favorable biodistribution and retention characteristics. Immunogenicity studies demonstrated that NanoVac-mediated delivery of HIV-1 trimer-encoding mRNA achieved robust antibody responses at substantially reduced mRNA doses, with low-dose formulations (0.1–1 μg/animal) producing responses comparable to those observed with a 30 μg dose. In addition, NanoVac alone stimulated T-cell responses, supporting its potential role as both a delivery vehicle and an immune-modulating component. These findings establish the manufacturing feasibility, pharmacokinetic profile, and dose-sparing potential of NanoVac, thereby supporting its further development as a scalable vaccine delivery platform for rapid-response applications.

item.title: The Role of Gly533 and Lys729 Residues in the Catalytic Activity and Friedelin Production of Monteverdia ilicifolia and Populus davidiana Synthases
item.description:
Abstract
Friedelin is a pentacyclic triterpene that exhibits a wide range of biological potential and is the precursor of bioactive quinonemethide triterpenes such as celastrol and pristimerin. This compound is synthesized by a specific oxidosqualene cyclase named friedelin synthase (FRS). This enzyme converts 2,3-oxidosqualene through rearrangement steps and promotes the production of a terpene with a ketone group at position C-3. Despite this, the precise mechanism of this oxidation remains unclear, highlighting the need to unveil FRS amino acid residues that are correlated with this specificity, catalytic efficiency, and friedelin production. For this reason, we performed site-directed mutagenesis in key residues and evaluated their production after heterologous expression in S. cerevisiaeusing GC-MS. Using multiple sequence alignment, we selected the residues Lys729, Tyr609, and Gly533 from Monteverdia ilicifolia FRS and correlated residues in Populus davidiana FRS for several mutations. Our results showed that the Lys729 residue is essential for enzyme activity and stability, while Tyr609 is not mandatory for friedelin production. Gly533Ala resulted in a notable improvement in the production of friedelin in MiFRS (3.633 ± 0.203 mg/L) and PdFRS (1.535 ± 0.169 mg/L) in comparison with wild type enzymes. Further molecular dynamics simulations showed that this particular mutation does not change significantly the structure of the enzyme but allows closer and stronger interactions that result in an increase in the amount of product formed by the mutant enzyme. In general, this work improves the understanding of residue interactions and shows a promising outlook for large-scale production of this compound.

item.title: Quantifying Cellular Nanoplastic Accumulation Using Raman Microscopy
item.description:
Abstract
Micro- and nanoplastic contamination poses emerging health risks through ingestion of contaminated food and water, thereby placing the intestinal barrier as the primary interface for nanoparticle translocation following ingestion. In this context, Caco-2 epithelial cells provide a well-established in vitro model of the small intestine barrier, yet label-free quantification of nanoparticle uptake at the single-cell level remains a significant methodological challenge in nanotoxicology. Here, we report a confocal micro-Raman spectroscopy strategy for per-cell quantification of polystyrene nanoparticle (150 nm diameter) accumulation in Caco-2 intestinal epithelial cells. Our approach combines ratiometric analysis, referencing the polystyrene marker band at ∼1002 cm–1 to the cellular amide I band at ∼1660 cm–1, with control-derived thresholding to distinguish cell-associated nanoparticles from endogenous phenylalanine background, followed by single-cell masking to compute quantitative uptake descriptors. Application to cells exposed to 16 and 25 μg/mL polystyrene for up to 24 h revealed concentration-dependent uptake dynamics. Whereas qualitative spatial occupancy suggests greater nanoplastic accumulation at the lower dose, a rigorous quantification─difficult to achieve with conventional fluorescence-based approaches─uncovers the true dynamics at both concentrations, reconciling apparently paradoxical trends with the complementary transcriptional response and cell viability assays presented herein. These findings demonstrate that the ratiometric Raman mapping framework proposed here provides a chemically specific and robust approach for studying nanoparticle–cell interactions relevant to nanoplastic risk assessment, suggesting that spatial organization of cell-associated nanoparticles as well as relative uptake burden may act as critical determinants of cellular bioactivity.

item.title: Applying the CO 2 -Based Mixture to Realize Efficient and Low-Cost Cooling for Deep Underground
item.description:
Abstract
The problem of heat hazard restricts the safe and efficient mining of deep mineral resources. A heat pump for simultaneous cooling and heating can control the heat hazard of deep mine and satisfy the heat load for mining community. However, the traditionally used working fluid of a heat pump, namely R22, possesses the disadvantages of being environmentally unfriendly and expansive operating cost. A CO2-based mixture is a promising substitute for R22 because of its excellent physical properties and great thermal match performance. This study carries out the thermo-economic analysis of a transcritical heat pump with the CO2-based mixture, and the feasibility of replacing R22 with the CO2-based mixture is investigated. The results show that the introduction of the CO2-based mixture can significantly cut down the irreversible loss in condensation and evaporation processes. R161 is the optimal additive for the CO2-based mixture, and the optimal COPc of CO2/R161 is 2.48, which is 12.2% higher than CO2 and 8.3% higher than R22. Although the initial capital cost of a heat pump with CO2/R161 is 24.2% higher than R22, the annual running cost is 6.39% less than R22, and substituting CO2/R161 for R22 can save operating cost by 1.62 × 106 CNY/year.

item.title: Selection of Anti-TIGIT Affibody Molecules Blocking the Interaction between TIGIT and CD155
item.description:
Abstract
T cell immunoglobulin and ITIM domain (TIGIT) is an immune checkpoint receptor expressed on T and NK cells that, upon interaction with its ligand CD155, suppresses immune cell activation. Tumor cells sometimes upregulate CD155 to evade detrimental immune reactions, and TIGIT is therefore an attractive target for the development of novel checkpoint inhibitor therapies. TIGIT has also been shown to be upregulated on tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), enabling imaging of TILs for patient stratification for immune checkpoint therapy. Here, we have selected so-called affibody molecules targeting TIGIT from a combinatorial affibody library displayed on the surface ofEscherichia coli. The two most promising candidates had equilibrium dissociation constants (KD values) of 2.5 and 6.5 nM, and were found to specifically interact with TIGIT-expressing cells. Furthermore, the affibody candidates were found to successfully block the interaction between TIGIT and CD155, suggesting future application as immune checkpoint inhibitors. Using an ensemble of general language models for in silico evolution, a variant with a 4.4 °C increased melting temperature could be derived, albeit with a 2-fold weaker affinity. The promising results justify further development of the anti-TIGIT affibodies for in vivo TIL-imaging and immune checkpoint therapy.

item.title: Thermal Phase Behavior, Structure, Acidity, and Quantum Chemical Insights into Novel Hydroxylamine Hydrochloride (HACl)-Methanesulfonic Acid (MSA) Deep Eutectic Solvents
item.description:
Abstract
The present study undertakes the first characterization of hydroxylamine hydrochloride (HACl)-methanesulfonic acid (MSA) deep eutectic solvents (DESs), a new generation of sustainable, dual-functional solvents with exceptionally strong acidic and inherently reduced properties. Employing FTIR, Raman, and NMR spectroscopy, the nature of HACl-MSA DESs’ molecular interactions was probed with varying molar ratios between 1:4 and 1:8. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) revealed composition-dependent phase behavior, transitioning from an amorphous glass-forming liquid at 1:4 (Tg = −89 °C, peak at 85.87 °C) to congruent melting at 1:5 (Tm = +5.43 °C). For 1:6 to 1:8 formulations, invariant eutectic behavior was observed with a shared solidus transition at about −53.80 °C and a clear melting range ending between −45.91 and −39.21 °C. Spectroscopic analyses confirmed the formation of a homogeneous, single-phase protic DES characterized by a robust, shielded hydroxylammonium core ([NH3OH]+) at 9.87–9.88 ppm and a dynamic acid proton pool that shifts downfield from 13.19 to 13.63 ppm. This shifting resonance directly reflects a tunable macroscopic acidity driven by the expansion of the MSA-MSA hydrogen-bonded network. Quantitative Hammett measurements (H0), determined via UV–vis spectroscopy, demonstrated significant acidity, reaching −6.116 at the 1:8 ratio. Density functional theory (DFT) analysis also confirmed the results, revealing a greater internal thermodynamic stability for the 1:5 ratio with a |ΔEint| = 4.280 eV. However, conceptual DFT descriptors, including a smaller energy gap (7.324 eV), a larger global softness value of 0.137 eV–1, and a more negative chemical potential (−4.506 eV), highlight the 1:4 ratio as a promising theoretical candidate for further evaluation in metal coordination processes. While these electronic metrics suggest a highly polarizable microenvironment, direct extraction yields, leaching kinetics, viscosity, and selectivity require future experimental validation. Through correlations established between molecular structure, frontier orbital analysis, and macroscopic Brønsted acidity trends, HACl–MSA DESs are highlighted as promising candidate platforms for potential application in hydrometallurgical leaching processes. However, definitive claims regarding selective metal extraction, long-term stability, recyclability, and environmental sustainability require comprehensive future experimental evaluation.

item.title: Nitrile-Based Leishmania Cysteine Protease B Inhibitors with In Vivo Efficacy against Visceral Leishmaniasis
item.description:
Abstract
Leishmaniasis remains a major neglected tropical disease with limited therapeutic options and increasing concerns regarding toxicity and drug resistance. Cysteine protease B (CPB), a key virulence factor in Leishmania spp., represents an attractive molecular target for the development of new antileishmanial agents. In this study, we designed and synthesized a series of dipeptidyl nitrile derivatives as reversible covalent CPB inhibitors and evaluated their biological activity in vitro and in vivo. Molecular docking performed in covalent mode demonstrated favorable accommodation of the compounds within the CPB active site, with the benzyl-containing derivatives showing the most favorable interactions. Among the series, compound 1 ((S)-tert-butyl (1-((cyanomethyl)amino)-1-oxo-3-phenylpropan-2-yl)carbamate) exhibited potent inhibition of recombinant LmCPB2.8ΔCTE (IC50 = 4.3 ± 0.2 μM) and strong activity against intracellular amastigotes of Leishmania infantum (EC50 = 3.9 ± 0.5 μM; SI ≈ 77) and Leishmania amazonensis (EC50 = 4.6 ± 1.6 μM; SI ≈ 65), surpassing miltefosine in selectivity. Compound 1 showed no cytotoxicity toward murine macrophages, no hemolytic activity, and good tolerability in the Galleria mellonella model. Oral administration of compound 1 to L. infantum-infected BALB/c mice (0.77 mg/kg/day for 5 days) resulted in a significant reduction in parasite burden in the liver and spleen (≈ 40–55%), even at a 10-fold lower dose than miltefosine. Although alterations in hepatic transaminases were observed, no evidence of renal dysfunction was detected. Collectively, these findings identify dipeptidyl nitriles as promising CPB-targeting scaffolds and position compound 1 as a lead structure for further optimization aimed at enhancing antileishmanial efficacy while minimizing host toxicity.

item.title: Thiochromene Analogues as Antiparasitic Chemotype: Synthesis, Antiplasmodial and Antitrypanosomal Profiling, Experimental Validation, and Computational Insights into Trypanothione Reductase Inhibition
item.description:
Abstract
The emergence of drug resistance and the limited availability of effective therapeutics continue to hinder the treatment of protozoal diseases, highlighting the need for new chemotypes with broad-spectrum antiparasitic potential. In the present study, a series of nitro and trifluoromethyl-substituted thiochromene carboxamides, previously identified as antileishmanial agents, were further explored for their broad-spectrum antiparasitic potential. Biological screening identified several compounds with promising activity and favorable selectivity against Plasmodium falciparum (D10 and W2 strains) and Trypanosoma brucei (AnTat1.1E strain). As the synthesized analogues exhibited a more favorable antitrypanosomal activity and selectivity profile, representative analogues were subsequently evaluated for trypanothione reductase (TryR) inhibition to investigate their potential mechanism of action, as TryR is a validated and highly conserved drug target across kinetoplastid parasites. Among the synthesized molecules, compound 5p showed the highest antiplasmodial potency (D10 EC50 = 2.1 μM), whereas compounds 5c and 5r were the most potent antitrypanosomal analogues (EC50 = 1.8 μM). Structure–activity relationship analysis demonstrated that piperidine and piperazine-containing carboxamide is a key pharmacophoric feature for broad-spectrum activity, whereas incorporation of a nitro substituent enhanced the activity against T. brucei. To investigate the potential mode of killing, representative compounds were evaluated for inhibition of TryR, identifying compound 5v as the most potent enzyme inhibitor. Enzyme kinetic studies established an uncompetitive mode of inhibition (ki ≈ 29.5 μM), suggesting interaction at an allosteric site rather than the active catalytic site. Consistent with these findings, SiteMap analysis identified a druggable allosteric pocket at the dimer interface of substrate-bound TryR, where the active compounds exhibited favorable binding affinities and interaction profiles. Collectively, these results demonstrate that thiochromene carboxamides constitute a promising scaffold for the development of broad-spectrum antiprotozoal agents and support allosteric inhibition of TryR as a viable strategy for antitrypanosomal drug discovery.

item.title: A Single Active-Site Water Molecule Encodes Two Distinct Proton-Coupled Electron Transfer Pathways in Fatty Acid Photodecarboxylase
item.description:
Abstract
Water molecules are key actors in enzymatic proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET), yet their mechanistic versatility remains underexplored. Using a multiscale computational approach, we show that a previously unidentified water molecule (Wat3) in fatty acid photodecarboxylase (FAP), a natural photoenzyme converting fatty acids into alkanes, mediates radical quenching via two PCET pathways: in the dominant one, which qualitatively agrees with the 100 ns experimental time scale, Wat3 stabilizes the transition state for direct proton transfer from Cys432 to the alkyl radical; in the alternative, the same molecule acts as a proton shuttle in a quasi-concerted two-proton transfer, with the flavin semiquinone providing the electron in both cases. The minor pathway, though less accessible in wild-type FAP, may become operative in engineered variants or related enzymes. Additionally, CO2 reacts with the thiolate to yield a thiocarbonate adduct, explaining unassigned crystallographic electron density. These results show how a single water molecule encodes mechanistic diversity in enzymatic PCET.

item.title: Probing Catalytic Residues Responsible for Primer Substrate Reactivity in a Versatile cis -Geranylgeranyl Diphosphate Synthase
item.description:
Abstract
Cis-isoprenyl diphosphate synthases (cis-IDSs) catalyze the synthesis of polyisoprenyl diphosphates with varying chain lengths and stereochemistry, yet the molecular mechanism underlying their substrate selectivity remains elusive. Here, we investigated VoDN3985, a cis-IDS from Viburnum odoratissimum, by combining mutagenesis, conditioned molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) calculations. Conditioned MD simulations revealed substrate-dependent differences in geometric preorganization, with geranyl diphosphate (GPP) showing the highest prereactive fraction and farnesyl diphosphate (FPP) sampling more idealized allylic torsional geometries than dimethylallyl diphosphate (DMAPP). Active-site substitutions at Asn64 and His79 expanded primer tolerance to enable DMAPP utilization while preserving concerted substitution pathways in QM/MM profiles. Crucially, selectivity shift from altered configuration-dependent reaction energetics rather than barrier reductions. By decoupling dynamic conformational preorganization from intrinsic reaction-path energetics, this study provides actionable mechanistic principles for rationally engineering cis-IDS substrate selectivity.

item.title: Genesis and Geological Significance of the Black Oil Reservoir with a Condensate Gas Cap in the Baijiantan Formation of Hefeng 3 Block, Junggar Basin, NW China
item.description:
Abstract
The Triassic Baijiantan Formation in the Hefeng 3 block, Junggar Basin, hosts an unusual hydrocarbon accumulation characterized by the coexistence of conventional black oil and a condensate gas cap within a single reservoir. This study integrates geochemical data, PVT simulations, and fluid inclusion analysis to unravel its genesis. Results show that the reservoir is a medium-porosity, ultralow-permeability system. The black oil originated from mature Fengcheng Formation source rocks, whereas the gas cap comprises mixed-source kerogen-cracking gases from both the Fengcheng Formation and Carboniferous sources. We propose a two-stage charging model: early accumulation of Fengcheng-derived black oil, followed by late injection of highly mature Carboniferous-derived dry gas. Evaporative fractionation induced by gas invasion transformed the original volatile oil into the present-day black oil–condensate gas cap configuration. This model challenges conventional single-source interpretations and provides a new genetic framework for complex fluid-phase reservoirs in the Junggar Basin. Our findings offer practical exploration guidance for similar composite reservoirs in superimposed basins worldwide.

item.title: Properties of Cellulose Nanocrystals Extracted Using Deep Eutectic Solvents
item.description:
Abstract
Cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) are biosourced colloidal building blocks that have attracted significant scientific attention due to their unique properties, such as high mechanical strength, biodegradability, nontoxicity, and potential for sustainable material development. Acidic hydrolysis utilizing strong acids, mainly sulfuric acid, remains the predominant method for CNC production on both laboratory and commercial scales. However, this approach involves challenges associated with the use of corrosive reagents, acid neutralization, and extensive purification. Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) have been proposed as alternative processing media for CNC extraction, with potential advantages including reduced reliance on concentrated mineral acids and opportunities for solvent recovery and recycling. Here, we report a detailed characterization of DES-extracted CNCs and their characteristics and properties contrasted with those of commercial acid-extracted CNCs. The DES-CNCs were dispersible but with lower ζ-potential and typically longer lengths, forming colloidal gels down to low concentrations that prevent the formation of liquid crystalline phases at higher concentrations, while ultrasound application and increased ionic strength were also found to promote aggregation. The mechanical response of these eutectic-extracted CNCs is followed by linear and nonlinear rheometry at different concentrations and is compared to that of commercial sulfuric acid-extracted CNCs.

item.title: Benchmarking SERS Platforms for Label-Free G-Quadruplex Analysis
item.description:
Abstract
Efficient adsorption of DNA onto metal nanoparticle surfaces is essential for an SERS-based structural analysis. However, the negative surface charge of commonly used nanoparticles promotes electrostatic repulsion with DNA, limiting adsorption and SERS enhancement and often requiring the use of aggregating agents. As Raman enhancement depends not only on the nanoparticle charge but also on the nanoparticle morphology, composition, and surface chemistry, systematic evaluation of nanoparticles with diverse physicochemical properties is necessary to identify optimal conditions for DNA adsorption and SERS detection. Metallic nanoparticles differing in metal (silver or gold), surface charge (positive or negative), and shape (spheres or stars) were synthesized by chemical reduction. To eliminate residual synthesis species, silver and gold nanospheres were also prepared by pulsed-laser ablation in liquid (PLAL). Eight nanoparticle types were characterized by UV/vis/NIR absorption spectroscopy, electrophoretic and dynamic light scattering, and scanning electron microscopy. Their SERS performance for DNA structural analysis was evaluated using the human telomeric sequence d[(TTAGGG)4] (Tel24), which adopted an antiparallel G-quadruplex (G4) in the presence of sodium ions (100 mmol/L), enabling comparison of nonfolded and folded DNA. SERS spectra were recorded with 532 and 785 nm excitation. Circular dichroism spectroscopy was used to confirm the DNA structures. Negatively charged citrate-stabilized silver and gold nanospheres (AgNP_cit and AuNP_cit) and silver nanostars (AgNS_cit) produced the most intense and structurally informative SERS spectra. Spectral markers, including shifts of guanine bands associated with Hoogsteen hydrogen bonding, bands assigned to G-tetrads and d(TTA) loops, and changes in adenine and guanine ring-breathing band intensities, clearly distinguished nonfolded from G4 DNA. The adenine-to-guanine intensity ratio (IdA/IdG) proved to be particularly sensitive to G4 formation. Despite being free of residual surface species, PLAL-prepared nanoparticles (AgNP_PLAL and AuNP_PLAL) showed a substantially weaker SERS enhancement. Likewise, positively charged spermine-coated nanoparticles (AgNP_sp and AuNP_sp) performed poorly, despite favorable electrostatic interactions with DNA. Near-infrared excitation (785 nm) was superior to 532 nm as visible excitation often produced interfering signals or no detectable spectra. Overall, citrate-stabilized silver nanospheres exhibited the best performance, providing reliable and intense SERS detection of both nonfolded and G-quadruplex Tel24. These findings provided practical guidelines for selecting SERS substrates and excitation wavelengths for distinguishing nonfolded DNA from G4 structures.

item.title: A Gradient Boosting-Based Machine Learning Model for the Prediction of the Hardness of Thermoplastic Polymers
item.description:
Abstract
Modern experimental techniques can measure the hardness of thin films and structural features on the nanometer scale. These techniques can be applied to many types of materials, but as the hardness of the material decreases, more specialized and precise equipment is needed. For polymers, this analysis can be relatively expensive and time-consuming, so here we demonstrate a gradient-boosting-based machine-learning model that can provide a fast and reliable prediction of the hardness of thermoplastic polymers. This model is based on the XGBoost algorithm and shows reasonably good performance with an R2 value of 0.46–0.69. The features used in this study include experimental (mechanical and thermal properties) and molecular descriptors obtained using RDKit. The model is robust, with reasonable performance obtained when key experimental features are removed and/or when the selection of polymers is reduced. This suggests that this approach will be useful in “bottom-up” strategies for polymeric materials development.

item.title: Long-Term Persistence of Encapsulated Facade Biocides and Their Transformation Products Is Associated with Shifts in Microbial Community Composition after Seven Years of Outdoor Weathering
item.description:
Abstract
Encapsulated biocides are widely used in polymer-based facade coatings to decrease microbial colonization, yet their long-term persistence and ecological effects remain poorly understood. This study investigated the fate of encapsulated terbutryn (TER), 2-octyl-1,2-thiazol-3-one (OIT), and 4,5-dichloro-2-octyl-1,2-thiazol-3-one (DCOIT) and their influence on microbial communities during a seven-year outdoor field trial using realistic facade systems. High-resolution LC-MS/MS revealed substantial residual biocide concentrations after weathering, with recovery rates of 31–51% for TER, 23–28% for DCOIT, and 8–19% for OIT. Several transformation products, including TER–OH, TER-DesE, TER–OH-DesE, TER-SO, TBM, and n-octylamine, were detected, demonstrating ongoing degradation processes within the facade matrix. Amplicon sequencing showed diverse bacterial and fungal communities despite persistent biocide residues. Community composition was significantly associated with biocide and transformation product profiles, and several dominant taxa exhibited compound-specific correlations. These findings demonstrate that residual biocides and their transformation products are significantly associated with long-term microbial selection on building facades.

item.title: High-Throughput Voigt Deconvolution of Luminescence Spectral Maps with Curvature-Informed Peak Initialization
item.description:
Abstract
Accurate deconvolution of overlapping emission bands remains a key challenge in luminescence spectroscopy, particularly for large-scale data sets generated by cathodoluminescence (CL) and photoluminescence (PL) mapping. This work presents a scalable Python-based workflow for high-throughput Voigt deconvolution of CL spectra. The approach integrates curvature-informed peak initialization with nonlinear least-squares optimization to improve fit stability and consistency across large data sets and extract quantitative spectral parameters, including emission energy, amplitude, and Gaussian and Lorentzian broadening contributions. The resulting parameters enable direct statistical analysis and spatial mapping across data sets. Synthetic validation and full-map uncertainty analysis show that peak center and total line width are more robustly recovered than the individual Gaussian and Lorentzian contributions when spectral features strongly overlap. Application to CdMgSeTe thin films demonstrates spatial variation in emission behavior and distinguishes differences in spectral heterogeneity between the analyzed films. This workflow enables high-throughput conversion of hyperspectral CL maps into spatially resolved spectral fingerprints with peak-level detail suitable for quantitative comparison across samples and processing conditions.

item.title: Study on Gas Production and Heat Transfer Characteristics of Underground Coal Gasification with Groundwater-Related Operating and Reservoir Factor Influence
item.description:
Abstract
Underground coal gasification (UCG) is the core technology for in situ clean conversion of deep coal resources, and one of its important differences from surface coal gasification is that the reaction process is significantly affected by groundwater. To address the insufficient consideration of groundwater effects in existing studies, the controlled retraction injection point technology-based multiphysics coupled numerical simulation model driven by partitioned reaction zone was established using COMSOL, and the reliability of the model was verified by pilot-scale tests. Then, the influences of three groundwater-related parameters, i.e., water injection flow velocity, coal seam permeability, and gasification pressure, on coal gas composition, temperature distribution, and heat-affected zone evolution were systematically investigated. The results show that the high-temperature zone and heat penetration depth are expanded by enhancing the water–gas reaction when the flow velocity is below the best-performing value of 0.55 m/min within the investigated range, and excessive heat absorption causes the maximum heat-affected depth to shrink sharply from 0.22 to 0.09 m when exceeding the threshold. Proper permeability improves gas–solid contact conditions, and the heat-affected thickness increases by over 175% at an optimal permeability of 6 mD among the tested points in this study, while excessively high permeability intensifies convective heat dissipation and reduces heat accumulation efficiency. The increase in gasification pressure significantly promotes CH4 enrichment, with the content increasing by more than 18 times as the pressure rises from atmospheric pressure to 8 MPa, and leads to the high-temperature zone and heat-affected zone being characterized by axial shrinkage and vertical widening. This study reveals the characteristics and mechanisms of heat transfer and gas production in the UCG process under the influence of groundwater-related factors, which can provide a scientific basis for the stable operation and thermal field regulation of UCG in deep coal seams.

item.title: Deciphering the Roles of Dispersed Solid Particulate Additives in THF Hydrate Induction and Crystal Growth
item.description:
Abstract
The unique structural characteristics of hydrates endow them with broad application prospects across various fields. However, the inherent stochasticity of nucleation induction time remains a primary obstacle to the commercialization of hydrate-based technologies. Encouragingly, some solid particles have been identified as effective kinetic promoters that can substantially shorten this induction period. To clarify the effect of particle properties on hydrate formation kinetics, this study systematically investigates the influences of nano-SiO2 (n = 9), SBA-15 (n = 14), and lignite (n = 21) on THF hydrate nucleation using a temperature-controlled optical microscopy system at −13 °C. The experimental results reveal that all three additives can reduce the THF hydrate nucleation induction time across repeated measurements, and the reduction trends vary with additive dosage. Within the tested mass concentration range, nano-SiO2, SBA-15, and lignite achieve maximum induction time reduction rates of 60.39%, 86.51%, and 94.33%, respectively. Among them, nano-SiO2 exhibits a nonmonotonic trend with an optimal nucleation mass concentration of 0.5 mg·mL–1. The promoting effect of SBA-15 gradually weakens as concentration rises, with its optimal induction time observed at 0.2 mg·mL–1. For lignite, hydrate nucleation is monotonically accelerated with increasing dosage. The hydrate promotion performance of these substances is governed by multiple factors. The proposed mechanisms, involving physical structure, pore confinement, and chemical composition, may provide references for interpreting the experimental observations.

item.title: Hydraulic Pressure and Sintering Temperature and Time Effects on the Performance of Niobium Selenide Designed as Microwave Resonators
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, niobium selenide powder ceramics in pellet forms are subjected to hydraulic pressure in the range of 50–200 bar, followed by sintering at temperatures of 200 and 400 °C. The sintering at 200 °C is performed for 1 and 20 h. The properties of these powder ceramics are explored by X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray fluorescence spectroscopy, and vector network spectroscopy in the range of 9 kHz to 6.0 GHz. It is observed that NbSe2 powder pellets prefer a hexagonal/trigonal structure comprising a minor phase of monoclinic NbSe3 (∼6%). Increasing the hydraulic pressure altered the structural parameters significantly, forcing denser pellets with relative density values reaching 96.8%. Sintering the pellets at 200 °C for 1 and 20 h highly improved the relative density up to 97.7%. Longer sintering time resulted in lower strain and fewer defects as compared to those in 1 h of sintering. In addition, SEM analyses show lamellar NbSe2 platelets, with the as-pressed samples being loosely stacked with high porosity and large pores, while 1 h sintering tightens contacts and refines pores, and 20 h sintering drops the porosity further. As microwave waveguides, NbSe2 pellets are tuned by the hydraulic pressure, showing resonance at 2.64 GHz with a bandwidth of 1.55 GHz, suiting 5G/6G technology applications. The short sintering time resulted in new resonance peaks at 3.24 and 4.29 GHz. The respective bandwidths are 2.25 and 1.80 GHz. The properties of NbSe2 powder pellets are promising as smart microwave resonators for high-frequency applications, including mobile networks.

item.title: Point Defect-Mediated Electronic Tuning and Thermal Stability of Carbon-Doped Boron-Nitride Fullerenes for Radical Scavenging
item.description:
Abstract
Reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (ROS/RNS) are involved in redox biology, but they remain challenging to control due to their high reactivity. This research evaluates the point defect-mediated electronic tuning of boron nitride fullerenes (BNFs) via progressive carbon (C) doping to enhance the scavenging of nitric oxide (NO) and superoxide anion (O2–). High-level density functional theory (DFT) calculations (ωB97X-D/6-311++G(d,p)) in gas and aqueous phases demonstrate that C-doping induces a transition from weak physisorption in pristine B12N12 to strong covalent chemisorption in C-doped systems when NO is adsorbed. Calculated thermodynamic functions support favorable adsorption of strongly bound complexes within the modeled temperature range. Pristine B12N12–NO remains unfavorable at 298 K. Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules, Electron Localization Function, and Localized Orbital Locator analyses reveal that localized spin density at the C-defect sites facilitates the formation of stable C–N and bridging C–O/B–O bonds. Finite-temperature stability was assessed using 300 K atomic density matrix propagation (ADMP) trajectories together with potential energy surface (PES)-based Langevin first-passage and mean first-passage time (MFPT) analyses. Adsorption produces system-dependent spectral redistribution, including selected near-ultraviolet/visible features and charge-transfer transitions. These results identify C-doped BNFs as theoretical metal-free radical-trapping platforms, while emphasizing the necessity of experimental validation before proposing biomedical or sensing applications.

item.title: Stimuli-Responsive Phenanthrene–Naphthol Fluorescent Marker for Security and Forensic Authentication
item.description:
Abstract
Smart functional materials with tunable optical features are highly attractive for anticounterfeiting and forensic applications. In this study, a phenanthrene–naphthol hybrid (PNH) was successfully synthesized and structurally characterized. PNH exhibited good solid-state fluorescence, photostability, intramolecular charge transfer characteristics, solvent-responsive luminescence, and aggregation-induced emission, along with reversible acido- and mechanofluorochromism. Quantitative pressure-dependent studies revealed a progressive and reproducible fluorescence response of PNH to mechanical stimuli. An eco-friendly water-based security ink with PNH as functional pigment was formulated, and the screen-printed patterns exhibited excellent UV stability and abrasion resistance. The prints enabled multimodal authentication through UV-induced fluorescence, reversible mechanical and acid/base vapor switching, and solvent-induced rear-side fluorescence. Notably, the chromic responses retained >90% of their initial fluorescence after 50 switching cycles, demonstrating excellent reversibility and operational durability. Further, PNH enabled high-contrast visualization of latent fingerprints on nonporous, semiporous, complex, and same-background substrates, facilitating the identification of level 1–3 ridge characteristics. Grayscale intensity profiling and three-dimensional surface mapping further confirmed enhanced ridge–furrow contrast and distinct ridge–valley morphology. Molecular dynamics simulations and spectroscopic analysis revealed favorable supramolecular hydrogen bonding and other noncovalent interactions between PNH and representative fingerprint residues, supporting its effective adhesion to latent-print ridges. Its forensic utility was further demonstrated for aged prints and samples exposed to elevated temperature and high relative humidity, where characteristic ridge and groove features remained discernible despite reduced fluorescence intensity. In addition, PNH facilitated clear visualization of groove patterns and minutiae in latent lip prints, indicating significant promise for cheiloscopic analysis. Comparative assessment with recently reported multifunctional fluorescent materials highlights the unique integration of AIE, reversible mechano- and acidofluorochromism, photostability, security-printing capability, and latent finger- and lip-print visualization in a single PNH fluorophore. Overall, PNH represents a versatile platform for next-generation security printing, anticounterfeiting, and forensic latent-print visualization.

item.title: Chemical Recycling of Poly(butylene adipate- co -terephthalate): A Glycolysis–Repolymerization Approach
item.description:
Abstract
Chemical recycling of bioplastics like poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT) promotes a circular economy by overcoming mechanical recycling limitations. This study investigated PBAT glycolysis and subsequent repolymerization of crude glycolyzed products, integrated with an early-stage life cycle assessment (LCA) using OpenLCA software with the ReCiPe 2016 Midpoint (H) impact assessment method to anticipate potential environmental impacts and sensitivity of the system. Glycolysis was conducted at 150–190 °C using Sn(Bu)2O (0.15 to 1.40 mol %) and NaHCO3 (5.0 mol %), presenting a Lewis acid coordination mechanism and a base-assisted glycolysis pathway, respectively, with ethylene glycol or 1,4-butanediol (4:1 molar ratio). Parameters including molar mass distribution (Mn, Mw, and Đ), species profile, and monomer yield were evaluated. Full conversion of the polymeric matrix was achieved within 2–5 h, leaving no detectable high-molecular-weight PBAT and yielding a mixture of oligomers and monomers, even at low catalyst concentrations (0.15 mol %), yielding oligomers with Mw of 0.6–1.4 kDa and up to 26.6 wt % monomer fraction. Notably, repolymerization without preliminary purification achieved Mw up to 10.6 kDa, comparable to 11.5 kDa reached using virgin raw materials. LCA results demonstrated improvements in 14 impact categories, with reductions between 6% and 35%. While fossil resource scarcity, ozone formation (human health and terrestrial ecosystem), and global warming potential increased due to the fossil-intensive energy baseline, the chemical proof of concept of directly utilizing crude glycolyzed products highlights the potential of this one-pot route to mitigate environmental burdens in polyester recycling, pending further property optimization.

item.title: Modular Solvent-Free Carbon Removal: A Solid–Sorbent Reactor for Sequential Direct Air Capture and Flue Gas Decarbonization
item.description:
Abstract
Scaling carbon removal to gigatonne-per-year levels requires capture technologies that are simultaneously efficient, environmentally clean, and deployable across heterogeneous emission sources, from dilute atmospheric CO2 (∼420 ppm) to concentrated industrial flue gas (1–33 vol %). Established amine- and hydroxide-based systems typically employ circulating liquid capture media and cyclic regeneration, making solvent handling, regeneration energy, and capture-medium degradation central to process complexity and economics. Here, an alternative solvent-free carbon capture process is demonstrated that addresses both source types within a single sequential platform. A composite sodium hydroxide–sodium percarbonate sorbent captures ambient CO2 via humidity-activated sodium peroxide (Na2O2) formation, fully converting NaOH to Na2CO3 with a capacity of 0.545 gCO2 gNaOH–1. The resulting carbonate is subsequently converted to bicarbonate under 15 vol % CO2 through water-mediated trona-phase growth, and is stacked in a modular reactor to achieve complete sequential capture at 0.612 gCO2 gsorbent–1. The end product, sodium bicarbonate, may be stored or used as feedstock for downstream electrochemical and chemical syntheses, offering a complementary solvent-free pathway for sequential carbon capture.

item.title: Programmable Twisting of Flexible Nanosurfaces with Attached Chiral Ligands
item.description:
Abstract
Chiral molecules attached to flexible nanoscale surfaces can interact cooperatively and deform their underlying surfaces in complex ways. Here, molecular dynamics simulations are used to model graphene ribbons with covalently attached chiral gluconic acid molecules in different crystal orders. The simulations revealed that asymmetric steric forces acting between the chiral molecules can generate stresses and torques that cause bending and helical twisting of the functionalized nanoribbons depending on their cut direction, relative sizes, ligand density, enantiomeric excess, and overall history. Upon annealing and quenching in water, the ligands can remain in the same crystalline phase, switch to a new phase, or become randomly oriented. Such deformable nanosystems can be implemented in sensing, mimicking, and memory applications.

item.title: Performance Evaluation of Lipopeptide-Enhanced Petroleum Sulfonate Binary Flooding System
item.description:
Abstract
To address the rapid interfacial activity decay and high adsorption loss of conventional chemical flooding under harsh reservoir conditions, this study developed an alkali-free biochemical binary composite system by partially substituting petroleum sulfonate with the biosurfactant lipopeptide (0.15 wt % petroleum sulfonate + 0.15 wt % lipopeptide + 1400 mg/L HPAM). Systematic thermal aging, emulsification, dynamic antiadsorption, and core flooding evaluations revealed distinct performance enhancements over the conventional chemical binary system. After 60 days of aging at 45–65 °C, the composite system sustained interfacial tension within the ultralow regime (10–2 mN/m) and exhibited a 20–28 percentage points higher viscosity retention rate, along with a counterintuitive decrease in equilibrium interfacial tension at elevated temperatures. In multicycle dynamic sand contact tests at 55 °C, competitive adsorption and steric/electrostatic shielding by lipopeptides prolonged the antiadsorption lifespan by an additional cycle. In physical core displacement experiments, the biochemical system achieved an incremental oil recovery of 6.1 percentage points over the conventional counterpart. These findings demonstrate that “structural and electrical complementarity” between biosurfactants and synthetic surfactants provides an effective, alkali-free route for chemical flooding in heavy oil reservoirs.

item.title: pH-Responsive Delivery of Nonsteroidal Anti-Inflammatory Drugs by ZIF-8 Metal-Organic Frameworks for Cancer Treatment
item.description:
Abstract
Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) have attracted increasing attention as potential anticancer agents due to their ability to inhibit cyclooxygenase-mediated inflammatory pathways involved in tumor progression. However, their clinical use in oncology remains limited by poor tumor selectivity and systemic toxicity. In this work, we investigate zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) nanoparticles as pH-responsive carriers for the delivery of different NSAIDs with potential anticancer activity. A loading strategy based on the conversion of the drugs into their sodium salts, followed by ultrasound-assisted encapsulation, was developed to preserve the structural integrity of the MOF while achieving efficient drug incorporation. Structural and textural characterization by XRPD, SEM, ATR-MIR spectroscopy, and nitrogen physisorption confirmed the formation of ZIF-8 nanoparticles with an average size of about 150 nm and the successful encapsulation of the drugs within the porous framework. High-performance liquid chromatography revealed drug-loading efficiencies exceeding 80% for selected formulations. Release studies demonstrated a pronounced pH-dependent behavior, with significantly faster drug release under mildly acidic conditions that mimic the tumor microenvironment. The biological activity of selected formulations was evaluated in prostate-derived cell models (BPH, LNCaP, and DU145), revealing enhanced cytotoxicity toward cancer cells under acidic conditions compared to physiological pH. In particular, naproxen@ZIF-8 showed a marked reduction in DU145 cell viability at low concentrations and under mildly acidic conditions. These results highlight the potential of ZIF-8 as a versatile nanoplatform for the controlled and tumor-responsive delivery of anti-inflammatory drugs with an anticancer activity.

item.title: Effect of CO 2 -Thermal Synergy on Nonlinear Percolation Behavior of Heavy Oil in Porous Media
item.description:
Abstract
As a greenhouse gas, CO2 can dissolve into heavy-oil systems through molecular diffusion and phase interactions, altering their rheological properties. It reduces steam consumption in the traditional thermal recovery of heavy oil. Clarifying the control laws of CO2-heavy oil interactions on flow characteristics in porous media has important significance for formulating enhanced oil recovery (EOR) schemes in high-viscosity reservoirs and achieving CCUS goals. This study focuses on ordinary heavy oil (OHO) and extra-heavy oil (EHO) from the J230 block of the Xinjiang Oilfield. Through systematic experiments and theoretical modeling, it comprehensively reveals the regulatory mechanisms of CO2 dissolution on the non-Darcy percolation characteristics of heavy oil. The results demonstrate that CO2 dissolution significantly reduces the viscosity, anomalous temperature, and yield stress of the heavy oil. The viscosity–temperature relationship follows an Arrhenius-type exponential model, based on which a viscosity prediction equation incorporating CO2 solubility was established. Percolation experiments show that CO2 can reduce the immobile area of OHO/EHO by 67.11–96.25%. On the basis of non-Darcy percolation theory, a power-law relationship between PTPG (pseudothreshold pressure gradient) and CO2 dissolution amount in double-logarithmic coordinates was derived, and a percolation capacity evaluation chart was constructed. On the basis of the quantitative analysis of the CO2-heavy oil seepage dynamic response, this study derived a theoretical drainage radius prediction equation after CO2 dissolution. Under idealized flow models and experimental conditions, the equation indicates that increasing the level of CO2 dissolution can significantly enhance drainage capacity, providing a theoretical reference for well spacing optimization. This study establishes, for the first time, a quantitative relationship model among CO2 solubility, PTPG, and drainage radius, providing theoretical guidance for CCUS and CO2-assisted steam flooding EOR technologies in high-viscosity reservoirs.

item.title: Pollution Characteristics and Health Risk Assessment of Potentially Toxic Elements in the Black Soil Region of Southern Jilin Province, China
item.description:
Abstract
To investigate the spatial distribution, pollution status, sources, and health risks of potentially toxic elements (PTEs) in the topsoil of three counties/cities (Shuangliao City, Lishu County, and Gongzhuling City) in southern Jilin Province, 138 topsoil samples (0–20 cm depth) were collected and analyzed for eight elements (As, Cd, Cr, Pb, Hg, Cu, Ni, and Zn). Spatial distribution patterns were examined using Kriging interpolation. Pollution levels were assessed via the single-factor pollution index, Nemerow comprehensive pollution index, and potential ecological risk index. Source identification was conducted by integrating correlation analysis, cluster analysis, and principal component analysis. Health risks for adults and children were quantified using the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) exposure model. The results showed average concentrations of 16.758 mg/kg for Cu, 21.415 mg/kg for Ni, 0.076 mg/kg for Cd, 47.161 mg/kg for Cr, 19.382 mg/kg for Pb, 16.681 μg/kg for Hg, 47.630 mg/kg for Zn, and 7.047 mg/kg for As. Spatially, the elements exhibited a pattern of “higher in the east, lower in the west”. Coefficients of variation indicated a strong variation for Hg, Cd, and As and moderate variation for the remaining elements, reflecting a notable anthropogenic influence. Pollution assessment revealed that the average single-factor pollution indices ranged from 0.007 to 0.235, and the Nemerow comprehensive pollution index was 0.694, corresponding to an overall nonpolluted status. The average potential ecological risk index (RI) was 73.417, indicating low ecological risk, with only 18.39 and 7.97% of samples showing moderate risk for Cd and Hg, respectively. Source analysis indicated that Cu, Ni, Cr, and Zn originated mainly from soil parent material (natural sources with minor human input), Cd and Hg derived primarily from agricultural fertilization, and Pb and As were associated with combined traffic and agricultural emissions. Health risk assessment showed an average non-carcinogenic hazard indices (HI) of 7.43 × 10–2 for adults and 4.18 × 10–1 for children (both <1), and average carcinogenic risks (TCR) of 3.81 × 10–5 for adults and 5.32 × 10–5 for children, all within acceptable ranges. Oral ingestion was the dominant exposure pathway (>90%), with As, Cr, and Pb as the main contributors to non-carcinogenic risk, and Ni, Cr, and As as the primary contributors to carcinogenic risk. In conclusion, the black soil region of southern Jilin Province exhibits low PTE pollution, low ecological risk, and controllable health risks.

item.title: Electrostatic Contribution of K339 to the Flavin Reduction of Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 d -2-Hydroxyglutarate Dehydrogenase
item.description:
Abstract
d-2-Hydroxyglutarate dehydrogenase from Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 (PaD2HGDH; EC 1.1.99.39; UniProt ID Q9I6H4) is a Zn2+- and FAD-dependent enzyme that catalyzes the oxidation of d-2-hydroxyglutarate to 2-ketoglutarate and has emerged as a potential antibacterial target. A fully conserved positive charge, K339 in PaD2HGDH, is located at the active-site entrance ∼2 Å from the substrate C5 carboxylate, where its positively charged side chain is poised to assist substrate binding via electrostatic interactions. To explore its mechanistic significance, K339 was substituted with methionine, glutamine, or arginine. Rapid-reaction kinetics revealed that K339 substitution weakened d-malate binding (Kd) by ∼5 kJ/mol, reflecting loss or partial attenuation of the electrostatic stabilization provided by the lysine side chain to the substrate C5 carboxylate. The rapid-reaction kinetics pH profile showed that loss of the K339 positive charge shifted the pKa of the Zn2+–OH(C2) substrate complex from 8.9 to 10.4, indicating less favorable deprotonation of the substrate C2 hydroxyl in K339 variants. The pH-independent rate constant for flavin reduction, kred, decreased by up to 80-fold (ΔΔG ∼ 11 kJ/mol) in K339 variants, consistent with the mutation altering the optimal orientation of the substrate C2 hydroxyl group required for flavin reduction. All K339 variants markedly impaired kcat and kcat/Km, revealing a ∼15 kJ/mol catalytic contribution, while viscosity effects indicated mutation-dependent perturbation of internal isomerization of the enzyme complex during turnover. Overall, K339 plays key electrostatic role in substrate binding and catalysis in PaD2HGDH, with important implications for enzyme engineering and the development of antibacterial inhibitors against P. aeruginosa.

item.title: Determination of 226 Ra in 225 Ac Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients by ICP-QQQ-MS
item.description:
Abstract
Growing demand for 225Ac-radiopharmaceuticals in targeted α therapy (TAT) has led to the development of new and diverse 225Ac manufacturing processes. While this has augmented global 225Ac supply, it has also created a need for common analytical methods to ensure 225Ac active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) meet uniform expectations for safety and efficacy. A particular challenge is the measurement of long-lived radionuclidic impurities (e.g., 227Ac, 226Ra, or 229Th). Many of the common radiometric techniques for radiopharmaceutical quality control suffer from poor sensitivity and long measurement times when applied to long-lived radionuclides. Mass spectrometry presents an attractive alternative owing to greater sensitivity for long-lived radionuclides and faster sample measurement. Several new 225Ac manufacturing processes use the long-lived radionuclide 226Ra as a starting material. This work reports a method for the determination of 226Ra in 225Ac APIs using triple quadrupole inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-QQQ-MS). The sensitivity and interference formation characteristics of multiple instrument modes (STD, KED, O2) were evaluated to identify the best configuration for 226Ra determination. The polyatomic ion 225Ac1H+ was identified as an interference at m/z = 226 in both STD mode and KED mode, however, the use of O2 as a reaction gas effectively removed this interference. Thus, the measurement of 226Ra at m/z = 226 → 226 in O2 reaction mode provided the best combination of sensitivity and specificity. This methodology was evaluated against appropriate criteria for accuracy, precision, specificity, linearity, and lower range limits. Accuracy and precision were evaluated by spike recovery studies using 226Ra spiked 225Ac API solutions. Spike recoveries were 85–114% for samples with 0.0500 to 0.997 ng L –1 of 226Ra. Repeatability (n = 6, one analysis) and intermediate precision (n = 12, two analyses) were evaluated by replicate determinations of 226Ra spiked samples (0.499 ng L–1) giving RSDs of 3.8% and 6.5%, respectively. The instrumental detection limit and quantitation limit were estimated to be 0.010 ng L–1 (0.36 Bq L–1) and 0.030 ng L–1 (1.1 Bq L–1), respectively. The proposed methodology allows for rapid, sensitive determination of 226Ra in 225Ac APIs. Implementation into 225Ac manufacturing processes will support high standards of product safety and efficacy.

item.title: Unveiling the Degradation of Methylammonium Lead Iodide (MAPbI 3 ) Perovskite under Simultaneous External Conditions
item.description:
Abstract
Metal halide perovskites have attracted significant attention for a broad range of optoelectronic and photonic applications due to their fascinating properties. Particularly, methylammonium lead iodide (MAPbI3) has shown specific promise for many applications, but its long-term stability remains a major challenge. This work systematically investigates the degradation pathway of MAPbI3 perovskite thin films under the combined effect of temperature (20–40 °C) and humidity (20–40%). We used a combination of advanced theoretical calculations and characterization tools to gain in-depth insight into the degradation mechanism of MAPbI3 perovskite. The findings reveal that increased temperature and humidity accelerate the decomposition of the perovskite structure, leading to the formation of degradation products such as PbI2, Pb(OH)I, and PbCO3. A clear trend in the degradation rate was observed, with the most severe degradation occurring under simultaneous high temperature and humidity. Quantitatively, under the maximum exposure condition (H40-T40), the MAPbI3 (110)/PbI2 (001) XRD intensity ratio dropped sharply from approximately 3.8 to near zero after 144 h. In contrast, under the H20-T20 condition, the ratio decreased gradually from 4.3 to 0.4 after a 240 h. These findings provide insights into the environmental degradation pathways of MAPbI3 thin films, highlighting the critical influence of temperature and humidity on their stability. Our computational calculations provide a molecular-level understanding of the mechanisms driving degradation.

item.title: Vanadium Occurrence and Enrichment Mechanisms in Lower-Middle Carboniferous Black Shales of the Central Taurus Belt, Türkiye: Insights into Critical Element Potential
item.description:
Abstract
Vanadium(V) is considered a critical metal due to its increasing use in low-carbon energy technologies, particularly V redox-flow batteries. Black shale-hosted deposits represent an important unconventional V resource, where enrichment is closely linked to depositional redox conditions, organic matter accumulation, and postdepositional processes. This study investigates Lower-Middle Carboniferous black shales from the Çavuşlar-Kırtıl (Mersin) regions in the Central Taurus Belt of Türkiye, which represent a notable occurrence of V enrichment. Using an integrated geochemical and mineralogical approach, this study constrains V sources, reconstructs paleo-redox conditions, determines host phases, and identifies the key controls on V enrichment. The studied black shales are composed mainly of quartz, calcite, feldspar, and Illite-dominated clay minerals, representing mixed mudstone lithofacies. TOC contents range from 1.72 to 2.79 wt %, whereas V concentrations vary between 411 and 615 ppm. EFs indicate moderate-strong enrichment of redox-sensitive elements (V–Mo–U). Multiple reliable paleoredox proxies (UEF, MoEF, VEF, and NiEF, Fe/Al, Th/U, and Corg/P) consistently indicate deposition under predominantly suboxic to anoxic conditions with intermittent euxinic episodes. Trace element source assessment based on Fe/Ti, Al/(Al+Fe), Eu/Eu*, and elemental relationships indicates predominantly nonhydrothermal and authigenic signatures, supporting a trustworthy interpretation of the paleodepositional environment. EPMA and SEM–EDS analyses reveal that V is heterogeneously distributed within the shale matrix and associated with both organic matter and illitic clay minerals. Positive TOC-redox-sensitive element correlations suggest that organic matter might be the control on V enrichment, while measurable V in Illite indicates partial diagenetic redistribution into clay minerals under oxygen-deficient conditions. Overall, the results provide new insights into shale-hosted V enrichment mechanisms and their regional metallogenic significance.

item.title: OPC3/LEW: A New Flexible Three-Site Water Model to Simulate Low-Electrostatic Environments
item.description:
Abstract
One of the main goals of computational simulations is to closely reproduce the environmental conditions in which biomolecules perform their physiological functions. However, the choice of water model is often based more on computational cost than on its effect on the molecular environment, as is the case with membrane proteins. These systems fulfill their biological function in low-polarity molecular environments that the most common or currently available water models do not reproduce accurately. In this work, we present a new flexible water model with three interaction sites that accurately represents the low-polarity electrostatic environment typically observed in the proximity of membrane systems. Using molecular dynamics simulations and based on the interaction parameters of OPC3, this new low-electrostatic water model (OPC3/LEW) reproduces dielectric constants close to 20. Following the methodology of Aguilar-Pineda et al. for developing low-electrostatic models by opening the H–O–H angle, the bulk density and surface tension of blood plasma under physiological conditions were selected as target properties. The performance of the OPC3/LEW model was validated by evaluating nine thermodynamic properties as a pure component and its ability to preserve helical structures as a solvating medium for eight amphipathic peptides. Outcomes were compared with those obtained using four water models with three interaction sites: OPC3, OPC3-B, SPC/E, and TIP3P. Findings show that the OPC3/LEW model reproduces several properties of bulk water more accurately than models such as SPC/E and TIP3P at the evaluated temperatures. However, its greatest strength lies in preserving the helical structures of peptides that otherwise would adopt disordered states. Although its main limitation is the geometry of its open structure, which makes the model somewhat unrealistic, the findings suggest that the OPC3/LEW model could be used in systems involving low-polarity environments, such as membrane proteins.

item.title: Beyond Redox Synergy: Role of Trivalent Cations in Ni-Based Layered Double Hydroxides for Peroxydisulfate Activation
item.description:
Abstract
The persistence of fluoroquinolone antibiotics in aquatic environments represents a growing environmental concern and requires efficient and scalable treatment strategies. In this study, ciprofloxacin degradation was investigated through persulfate activation by using Ni-based layered double hydroxides (LDHs). NiFe-LDHs with different molar ratios (1:1, 2:1, and 3:1) were synthesized and compared with NiAl-LDH to elucidate the role of the trivalent metal in the catalytic performance. A 22 factorial design was employed to evaluate the influence of the catalyst dosage and persulfate volume. All catalysts exhibited rapid removal, reaching approximately 57% removal within 20 min and up to 87% removal after 120 min. Increasing the Ni content did not improve the overall removal performance, indicating that activity is not directly governed by the amount of Ni present. Kinetic analysis followed pseudo-second-order behavior, while factorial results indicated that catalyst dosage had a stronger influence than the persulfate concentration. Mass spectrometry confirmed the disappearance of the parent ion (m/z 332), indicating an effective transformation of ciprofloxacin. Radical scavenger experiments indicated a greater contribution of radical species in the Fe-containing materials, whereas NiAl-LDH showed a more adsorption-driven removal pathway. No synergistic enhancement between Ni and Fe was observed, as NiAl-LDH exhibited comparable or superior performance despite containing the non-redox-active Al3+ center. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed that Ni centers play a dominant role in persulfate activation, whereas the trivalent metal primarily modulates the electronic structure and the reaction pathway of the catalyst. These findings challenge the conventional assumption that the presence of multiple redox-active metal centers necessarily enhances the catalytic performance in LDH systems and highlight the critical role of the local electronic environment in designing efficient catalysts for environmental applications.

item.title: Temperature-Dependent Enzyme-Ligand Recognition Emerges from the Coupling of Protein Dynamics and Hydration
item.description:
Abstract
Protein–ligand interactions are governed by a subtle interplay between binding thermodynamics, protein dynamics, and hydration. However, how these factors are coupled remains poorly understood, particularly for enzymes whose function depends on coordinated water rearrangements. Here, we investigate the binding of the fluorinated sulfonamide inhibitors 4-fluorobenzenesulfonamide (4FBS) and pentafluorobenzenesulfonamide (PFBS) to the zinc metalloenzyme bovine carbonic anhydrase (BCA) at 298 and 308 K. Binding thermodynamics were characterized by isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC), while quasi-elastic neutron scattering (QENS) was employed to probe ligand-induced changes in protein dynamics. ITC measurements in D2O were complemented by measurements in H2O over 288–318 K to assess temperature and solvent isotope effects. PFBS binds more strongly to BCA than 4FBS over the entire temperature range, whereas the thermodynamic parameters are similar in H2O and D2O. QENS-derived estimates indicate that binding of either ligand increases the conformational entropy of BCA. In contrast to the thermodynamic trends, however, the dynamic response depends strongly on the ligand: the diffusion coefficient associated with localized internal motions decreases with increasing temperature for the BCA-PFBS complex but increases for BCA-4FBS, indicating that the two ligands modulate the protein energy landscape in distinct ways. Despite their closely related structures, PFBS and 4FBS exhibit markedly different temperature-dependent effects on BCA dynamics. Our results show that subtle changes in ligand chemistry can reshape the balance between protein flexibility, hydration, and binding thermodynamics.

item.title: DC Magnetron-Generated Reactive Glow Discharge Plasma Activation of Acid-Etched Titanium for Superhydrophilic TiO 2 -Rich Surfaces
item.description:
Abstract
This study addresses the need for controllable physicochemical activation routes for titanium surfaces by developing a hybrid treatment that combines hydrofluoric acid (HF) microtexturing with reactive glow discharge plasma (GDP) generated in a DC magnetron sputtering (DC-MS) system, applied to commercially pure grade 1 titanium. Sequential acid etching induced controlled microstructural roughening, followed by a 1 min plasma exposure in air at 6 × 10–1 Pa to modify the near-surface oxide chemistry while preserving the etched morphology. Acid treatment preferentially dissolved the α-Ti matrix along grain boundaries, producing band-like corrosion grooves and hierarchical microtexturing, whereas plasma activation induced localized oxidation and produced a superhydrophilic response. Eight activation cycles over 150 days of ambient storage repeatedly restored the hydrophilic state, which persisted approximately 16 h per cycle. Raw X-ray diffraction (XRD) and grazing-incidence XRD patterns remained dominated by α-Ti, with no resolved reflections attributable to crystalline TiO2. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy indicated the formation of a TiO2-rich surface after plasma activation, accounting for 100% of the fitted Ti 2p area, with no detectable F 1s signal. Adsorbed oxygen-containing species accounted for 4.7%, compared with 4.3% for the etched and 17.4% for the cleaned control. Because biological responses were not evaluated, these physicochemical changes should not be interpreted as direct evidence of improved protein adsorption, cellular behavior, bacterial resistance, or in vivo performance. This approach establishes DC-MS-generated GDP activation as a rapid route for titanium surface activation and advanced surface-engineering applications.

item.title: Comparative Study of Properties and Cytotoxicity of Eco-Friendly AgInS 2 , CuInS 2 , and ZnIn 2 S 4 Quantum Dots under a Unified Experimental Framework
item.description:
Abstract
Ternary quantum dots (TQDs) are promising cadmium-free nanomaterials for optoelectronic and biomedical applications; however, systematic comparisons among AgInS2 (AIS), CuInS2 (CIS), and ZnIn2S4 (ZIS) quantum dots remain limited because these materials are typically investigated using different synthetic protocols and characterization methodologies. Herein, we present a systematic comparative study of aqueously synthesized AIS, CIS, and ZIS quantum dots, enabling direct comparison of their optical, electrochemical, surface, and biological properties within a unified comparative framework. The nanocrystals exhibited similar sizes (4–6 nm), ensuring that the observed differences primarily reflected composition. Combined optical and electrochemical analyses revealed consistent trends in bandgap energies that were in good agreement with Mulliken electronegativity-based predictions. Despite their structural similarity, AIS showed long lifetimes and moderate emission efficiency, CIS exhibits suppressed photoluminescence due to dominant nonradiative recombination, whereas ZIS exhibited fast recombination dynamics associated with surface-dominated states. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy established a direct relationship between composition, defect states, and electronic structure, while all QDs exhibited high cell viability (>90%), confirming their cytocompatibility. Overall, this unified comparative approach demonstrates that cation identity governs band alignment, recombination pathways, and cytocompatibility, providing practical guidance for the rational design of cadmium-free quantum dots for photocatalytic, optoelectronic, and biomedical applications.

item.title: USP Standards for Dietary Ingredients Derived from Mate and Guayusa Leaves: A Quality by Design Approach to Method Development and Validation for the Simultaneous Determination of Methylxanthines and Hydroxycinnamoylquinic Acids
item.description:
Abstract
Mate (or yerba mate, Ilex paraguariensis) and guayusa (Ilex guayusa), both members of the Aquifoliaceae family and traditionally consumed as herbal teas in South America, are rich in methylxanthines and hydroxycinnamoylquinic acids that may provide stimulant and antioxidant properties for use in beverages and dietary supplements. This work demonstrates an analytical quality-by-design (AQbD) approach to developing a UHPLC method and sample preparation procedure for the simultaneous quantification of these compounds in mate and guayusa leaves and their extracts. Using AQbD principles, critical method attributes and parameters were defined and optimized through design of experiments to understand variable interactions, establish robustness within the method operable design region, and experimentally confirm the selected conditions. The resulting UHPLC-DAD method separates three methylxanthines and nine hydroxycinnamoylquinic acids within 12 min and was validated per ICH and USP <1225> guidelines, demonstrating specificity, linearity, precision, accuracy, robustness, and reliable relative response factors. Overall, the AQbD framework enabled the development of a robust method suitable for determining these analytes in a variety of dietary ingredients derived from Mate and Guayusa leaves.

item.title: Electrical and Thermal Transport in CaCO 3 Graphene Nanocomposites Derived from Oyster Shell Waste
item.description:
Abstract
Waste oyster shells provide a calcium carbonate, as Mg-calcite, feedstock for functional mineral composites. Here, shell-derived biogenic calcium carbonate (BCC) and few-layer graphene (FLG; nominally 1, 5, 7, and 10 wt % relative to BCC) were processed by aqueous planetary ball milling with Pluronic P123. Microscopy, diffraction, spectroscopy, thermogravimetry, and transport measurements were combined to examine the resulting powders and pressed pellets. Mg-calcite nanocrystallites and graphene sheets coexisted within micrometer-scale aggregates, with mineral particles preferentially observed near sheet edges. At 25 °C, the thermal conductivity of the 10 wt % formulation was 0.516 W·m–1·K–1, compared with 0.194 W·m–1·K–1 for the dry-milled shell. This approximately 166% reference-to-composite difference combines changes in composition and processing and cannot be assigned to FLG addition alone. Stable electrical measurements were obtained from 5 wt % FLG; the reported resistivity of the 10 wt % formulation was approximately 0.50 Ω·cm. The shell organic matrix may contribute to interfacial interactions, although its effect cannot be distinguished from those of Pluronic and processing in the present experiments. The observed transport differences among the prepared formulations provide a basis for future studies using matched processing controls to clarify the contribution of each constituent.

item.title: Photothermal-Augmented Cascade Catalysis: Engineering Nanozymes for Tumor ROS Burst Therapy
item.description:
Abstract
Nanozyme-based catalytic therapy triggered by tumor-specific endogenous stimuli is an emerging tumor therapy that has attracted significant attention. Nevertheless, the efficacy of current catalytic therapies is severely limited by the intrinsic catalytic efficiency of nanozymes and the low concentration of endogenous substrates. Herein, a novel and efficient CuS-COF@PDA/Apt-A/GOx (Cu-CPAG) nanozyme was rationally designed with multiple enzyme-like catalytic activities and an augmented photothermal effect. Meanwhile, the nanozyme could ingeniously bind to the overexpressed MUC1 protein in MCF-7 cells, thus effectively addressing the critical limitations of conventional catalytic therapy. Following targeted internalization, glucose oxidase (GOx) within the nanozyme catalyzes the oxidation of glucose to elevate endogenous hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) levels in tumor cells and trigger a cellular starvation effect. Then, the accumulated H2O2 is subsequently converted by CuS NPs into highly cytotoxic hydroxyl radicals (•OH), which significantly promotes the intracellular accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) in a cascade manner. Notably, owing to the excellent photothermal properties of CuS NPs and polydopamine (PDA), near-infrared laser irradiation exerts a distinct photothermal-augmented effect to further enhance the overall catalytic efficiency of the nanozyme, thereby inducing an amplified ROS burst in tumor cells. Consequently, the designed Cu-CPAG nanozyme can disrupt redox homeostasis in the tumor region through a photothermal-augmented cascade reaction, effectively overcoming the shortcomings of traditional nanozyme catalytic therapy. This work develops a promising strategy for cascade catalytic tumor therapy and provides valuable insights for the advancement of future biomedical applications.

item.title: Highly Luminescent Alkyl- and Alkoxy-Terminated Silicon Quantum Dots via Aging Following Single-Step Plasma Synthesis and Functionalization
item.description:
Abstract
Nonthermal plasma synthesis enables the continuous production and immediate surface functionalization of silicon quantum dots (Si QDs) in a single, flow-through reactor. While this process occurs on a millisecond time scale, the resulting nanocrystals are often limited by low photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQY) due to persistent surface defects. In this work, we demonstrate that a minimal post-treatment, aging the Si QDs in specific solvents, can enhance the PLQY to ∼50%, approaching the performance of much more complex solution-phase methods. We find that the choice of the surface ligand and solvent is critical: hexanol-terminated Si QDs exhibit significantly higher initial and final PLQYs than decene-terminated particles, likely due to the faster reaction of alcohols with electrophilic surface sites in the gas phase. Among the solvents investigated, chloroform consistently yields the highest PLQY. Furthermore, we show that light irradiation at 400 and 633 nm drastically accelerates the Si QD aging process, reducing the aging time from hundreds of hours to under 20 h. This practical “synthesize and forget” strategy offers an efficient pathway for optimizing high-PLQY Si QDs for applications in optoelectronics and bioimaging.

item.title: Effect of Low-Frequency Pulsating Water Injection Parameters on Coal Permeability: Quantitative Characterization Experiments and a Field Case Study
item.description:
Abstract
Efficient stimulation of coal reservoirs is crucial for enhancing coalbed methane (CBM) well productivity. As an emerging unconventional stimulation technology, low-frequency pulsating water injection (LF-PWI) has attracted widespread attention for its ability to transform the pore-fracture system of coal reservoirs and its potential for engineering application. In this study, LF-PWI experiments are conducted using NMR, CT, and a triaxial apparatus to investigate the influence of LF-PWI parameters on pore-fracture properties of coal samples. The dynamic gray relational analysis (DGRA) method is employed to quantitatively evaluate the correlations of pore-fracture properties with porosity and permeability, respectively. Finally, the stimulation mechanism of productivity is elucidated and validated through a case study. The results demonstrate that LF-PWI can reduce the coal elastic modulus by 35.15%. The volume and connectivity of micropores and mesopores fluctuate, while macropores with diameters of 200–300 μm increase significantly, forming dominant flow pathways (>500 μm). Permeability continuously increases due to macropore development (k/k0 = 4.07). Porosity initially shows a rapid rise driven by macropore expansion (φ/φ0 peaks near 1.05); it then declines (by up to 9.95%) and gradually recovers toward unity as the micropores vary. Increasing the pressure amplitude simultaneously enhances the deterioration of mechanical properties, the fluctuation of porosity, and the improvement of permeability. A segmented control strategy employing high–medium–high pressure amplitude can help balance the pore-fracture network, preserve the gas source, and expand gas seepage pathways. Field application in the DFZ-1 well confirmed that LF-PWI mitigates coal fines flowback and increases cumulative gas production by 17.07%. This study provides a theoretical basis for employing LF-PWI to improve CBM well productivity.

item.title: Oblique Back-Illumination Microscopy Enables Phase-Gradient Optical Sensing of Malaria-Induced Intracellular Heterogeneity
item.description:
Abstract
Malaria remains a major global health burden, with diagnosis often relying on ex vivo analysis of infected red blood cells (RBCs), which incompletely samples key stages of parasite development. In particular, early ring-stage parasites exhibit subtle structural perturbations, while a significant fraction of parasite burden─including immature gametocytes─is sequestered within the microvasculature and is not readily captured in peripheral blood smears. Here, we present a label-free imaging and analysis framework that integrates oblique back-illumination microscopy (OBM) with data-driven classification to detect malaria infection by sensing parasite-induced intracellular heterogeneity. Unlike stained brightfield microscopy and quantitative phase imaging (QPI) methods that depend on interferometric acquisition and phase reconstruction, OBM directly converts intracellular refractive-index gradients into measurable intensity variations through noninterferometric phase-gradient contrast. By exploiting multiply scattered illumination and asymmetric detection, OBM enhances sensitivity to parasite-induced refractive-index gradients associated with Plasmodium falciparum development, capturing morphological complexity across the intraerythrocytic lifecycle. This enables the discrimination of uninfected cells, early ring-stage infections, and mature gametocytes. Fourier-domain analysis further reveals infection-stage-dependent redistribution of spatial-frequency content, providing a physically interpretable description of progressive intracellular remodeling during parasite development.
